## Open a movie and start cutting

**File ▸ Open…** (⌘O) on a `.mov` or `.mp4` — or a drop on the Dock icon, or
**Open Video…** in the Welcome window — creates an *untitled* project sized and
rated to that file, with the file as the first clip on Track 1, ready to cut. A
portrait phone clip opens portrait, and a 29.97 fps file stays 29.97. **Save**
then writes a `.framejob` package, offered next to the source.

## Features

**Projects and media.** Movies, sound and pictures from everything macOS plays,
plus WebM and MKV copied in without re-encoding; missing files relinked;
Consolidate Media copies footage into the package.
→ [Projects and media](docs/guide/projects-and-media.md)

**Timeline.** One kind of track that holds any clip; a frame-accurate ruler,
filmstrips and waveforms, zoom about the cursor, snapping, markers, an in/out
range, track mute, solo, lock, volume, pan, compressor and limiter, clip names
and colour labels.
→ [The timeline and playback](docs/guide/timeline.md)

**Editing.** Move, nudge, trim, slip, roll, split, lift, ripple delete, close
gap, insert time, insert and overwrite, copy and paste, Paste Attributes, and
nests that group clips into one.
→ [Editing clips](docs/guide/editing.md)

**Canvas and layers.** Move, scale, rotate and crop on the preview; opacity,
blend modes, shadows, filters, chroma key, spotlight and obscure; text, shape,
image and background clips; matte tracks that cut the track behind them.
→ [Canvas, layers, text and shapes](docs/guide/canvas-and-layers.md)

**Motion and transitions.** Actions that ease any property to a new state over
a span — Zoom to Region for screencasts — motion presets for entrances, exits
and continuous movement, and thirteen transition styles.
→ [Motion, actions and transitions](docs/guide/motion-and-transitions.md)

**Speed.** Constant speed or fit to a length, ⌥-drag rate stretch, keep pitch,
reverse, freeze frame, and speed ramps — **Clip ▸ Speed Ramp…** makes a Ramp
Up, Ramp Down, Speed Dip or Speed Burst in one step.
→ [Speed, reverse and freeze frames](docs/guide/speed.md)

**Audio.** Per-clip volume, drawn as a line on each clip that you drag and
⌥-click to add points, fades in four shapes, ducking for a clip's length
or only while its speech plays, voice isolation (Apple's on-device voice model,
which also reduces room echo), sixteen voice effects (pitch, robot, telephone,
radio, echo, reverbs and more), channel selection, EQ with voice presets, hum
removal, noise reduction, a gate for the pauses, a leveller that evens out a
speaker who moves on and off the mic, phrase by phrase, and a de-esser, each
set from the clip's own loudness, compressor, pan, mono and a true-peak limiter, each
of them animated by actions as the volume is; each
clip's loudness and true peak in the inspector; Enhance Voice, which sets a
voice recording up for speech from its own measurements in one step; Match
Audio, which gives clips another clip's loudness and speech tone; and
Normalize to a loudness
target (−16 LUFS at −1 dBTP by default, turning the
limiter on when a clip's peaks need it) or to a peak, which matches clips; a
live loudness meter for the mix as it plays; Synchronize Audio lines up a
camera and a separate recorder by their sound, drift included. Detach Audio
keeps the sound linked to its picture, so J- and L-cuts stay in sync through
every edit, and Attach Audio puts it back.
→ [Audio](docs/guide/audio.md)

**Clean-up tools.** Remove Silences cuts dead air by voice or by level; Remove
Filler Words cuts the ums and uhs on their own timings. Both preview the cuts
and make them as one undo step.
→ [Remove Silences and Remove Filler Words](docs/guide/cleanup-tools.md)

**Captions.** Import SubRip, export SubRip or WebVTT; generate captions on this Mac
or with AssemblyAI, as two-line subtitles or word-by-word captions in five
styles. Every caption is an ordinary text clip.
→ [Captions and transcription](docs/guide/captions.md)

**Colour grading.** Light and colour controls, three wheels, curves, eight
built-in looks and your own `.cube` LUTs, adjustment clips with qualifiers,
Show Ungraded, and waveform, parade, vectorscope and histogram scopes.
→ [Colour grading](docs/guide/color-grading.md)

**HDR and colour management.** iPhone HDR, HDR10, wide gamut and camera log
read as what they are; SDR or HDR (HLG) projects; HLG, HDR10 and SDR-version
deliverables, with Show SDR Version to preview the last.
→ [HDR and colour management](docs/guide/hdr-and-color.md)

**Motion graphics.** Graphic clips drawn every frame by a small JavaScript
module: 23 built-ins, browsed by category with a live looping preview in the
Graphic dialog: charts, a gauge and timers, screencast keys and window
frames, title, quote and logo cards, and social pop-ups; properties as
inspector controls, your own modules too, each saved to share as a
`.fjgraphic` file with only the fonts and pictures it uses, which Frame Job
opens to import into a project.
→ [Motion graphics](docs/guide/graphics.md)

**Screen recording.** A display or a window, with system audio, microphone and
click rings, at 30 or 60 fps, into a new project or at the playhead; a camera,
on its own or beside the screen as a corner talking head; or a
microphone-only voice-over.
→ [Screen recording](docs/guide/screen-recording.md)

**Export.** H.264, HEVC (8-bit, 10-bit, with alpha), AV1 in MP4 or WebM
(10-bit, with HDR, from its own encoder built in, at three speeds; Opus sound
in the WebM), VP9 in WebM for every browser (8-bit, or 10-bit with HDR, also
built in, with Opus) and with alpha for transparent web video, ProRes 422 and 4444,
M4A, WAV and AIFF (16- or 24-bit, with stems: a file per track beside the
mix), GIF and animated PNG; loudness targets
reached through a true-peak master limiter on every export, presets, an Export
Queue that runs while you edit, and single frames as stills.
→ [Exporting](docs/guide/export.md)

**The Assistant.** A conversation with Claude in the inspector that edits the
open project with the same tools an agent uses, asks before it writes a file,
and shows what each turn cost.
→ [The Assistant](docs/guide/assistant.md)

**Agents over MCP.** The whole editor as MCP tools — one per edit plus open,
save, render a frame, export and the rest — for Claude Code or any MCP client.
→ [Driving Frame Job from an AI agent](docs/guide/mcp.md)

Also: [Settings](docs/guide/settings.md) and
[Menus and keyboard shortcuts](docs/guide/menus-and-shortcuts.md).

## Getting Frame Job

The newest signed and notarized build is always at
<https://github.com/kpgalligan/framejob/releases/latest/download/FrameJob.dmg>.
Open the DMG and drag Frame Job to Applications. An installed copy
updates itself (Frame Job ▸ Check for Updates…, [Settings](docs/guide/settings.md#updates)).

To build it yourself, see [Developing Frame Job](docs/developing.md).

## Using it with an AI agent

Frame Job serves its editor as MCP tools on a local socket only programs you
run can open. An MCP client reaches it through `framejob-mcp`, a helper inside
the app, which starts Frame Job in the background on the first tool call if it
is not running. **Frame Job ▸ Settings… ▸ MCP ▸ Copy MCP Command** puts the
Claude Code registration line on the clipboard, with your copy's path:

```sh
claude mcp add --scope user framejob -- '/Applications/Frame Job.app/Contents/Helpers/framejob-mcp'
```

[MCP](docs/guide/mcp.md) covers other clients and every tool;
[the Assistant](docs/guide/assistant.md) is the same tools inside the window.

# 1. What this is

A screencast editor without a recorder — and, since road map 3,
a recorder of the SCREEN, and since §11 CAM-1 of a camera beside it or on its
own, whose output is ordinary media. Open one or
more video files from disk, arrange them on layered tracks over a fixed canvas, trim,
split, annotate, animate, and export. Mac only, Apple Silicon, macOS 26+.

The bar is a balance: enough to make a real cut with text,
shapes, transitions and simple animation, without Final Cut's magnetic
timeline, roles, multicam, scopes, or a plugin ecosystem.

Deliberate non-goals: multicam, color grading beyond
per-clip controls (§11 GR-1: tier 1 of grading — tone, adjustment clips,
looks, LUT import, an ungraded switch and one luma waveform — is in, kept by
the owner's verdict of 2026-10-10, and tier 2's scopes, colour wheels,
curves and qualifiers beside it, GR-10…GR-13; tier 3's HDR→SDR conversion
and camera log are in, GR-15, GR-16; the HDR road map's HLG timeline, its
HLG, HDR10 and SDR-version deliverables, HDR scopes, the PQ peak, Canon Log
2 and 3 and opt-in linear-light blending are in, HD-1…HD-17; a wide-gamut
working space for SDR projects is not wanted, GR-20; tier 4's vectorscope zoom,
hue curves, the blend between curves of different point counts and the
qualifier's cleanup blur are in, GR-24, GR-31…GR-35, while an Offset
wheel, a qualifier on picture clips, 1,024-level scopes and a histogram
behind the curves are not wanted, GR-27…GR-30), a plugin system (a clip may
draw itself from a JavaScript module in its package, road map 10; nothing
else is scriptable — §11 G-1),
motion blur, stabilisation, optical-flow retiming and auto-reframe (heavy
pixel work or ML, outside the compositor's one-pass shape — road map 2 §4),
any platform but macOS. **Screen recording was on this list until road map 3
reversed it** (§11): the app records a display or a window through
ScreenCaptureKit into a file it then imports exactly as File ▸ Open would —
paused and resumed from the menu bar, each stretch its own file and its own
clip; callouts reconstructed after the fact stay out. **Camera recording
was on it too until §11 CAM-1** (road map "camera-recording") reversed it: a
camera alone or beside a screen recording, each its own file and clip.
**Audio beyond what shipped was on it too until §11 AU-2** (road map
"audio", 2026-10-30) lifted it: EQ, track and bus processing, and Apple's
built-in audio units are in, beside Frame Job's own DSP; hosting
third-party Audio Unit plug-ins stays out, under the plugin system above.

docs/guide/audio.md:92:- **⌥-click the line** to add a point there. A point is an action, not a keyframe: Frame Job adds an action that runs from the end of the previous action (or the clip's start) to where you clicked, ending at the level the line already has there, so the click on its own changes nothing you hear. Keep the mouse down and drag to move the new point's level. Inside an action that changes only the volume, the click splits that action in two at the point instead. Both halves keep its curve, so a linear action sounds the same until you drag, while an eased one is eased again on each side of the point. The click beeps, and adds nothing, inside an action that also changes something else or that runs past the clip's end (as one can after a trim), or within one frame of the start of the action it is in or of the previous action's end. Adding a point is one undo step, "Add Volume Point".

# Frame Job User Guide

Frame Job is a native macOS video editor for Apple Silicon Macs running
macOS 26 or later. You open a movie, arrange it on layered tracks over a fixed
canvas, then trim, cut, grade, caption, animate and export it. Every edit you
make in the window can also be made by an AI agent over MCP, or by the built-in
Assistant.

The quickest way in: **File ▸ Open…** (⌘O) on a movie makes an untitled project
sized and timed to it, with the movie on Track 1, ready to cut. Save writes a
`.framejob` package.

## The pages

Read the first four in order to learn the editor; the rest stand alone.

1. [Projects and media](projects-and-media.md) — starting, saving and opening projects, the `.framejob` package, the Document tab's canvas settings, importing files, the Media tab and relinking.
2. [The timeline and playback](timeline.md) — the editor window, tracks and their switches, the ruler and playhead, zoom, selection, snapping, markers, the in/out range and playback.
3. [Editing clips](editing.md) — placing, moving, trimming, slipping, splitting, deleting and closing gaps, copy and paste, and nests.
4. [Canvas, layers, text and shapes](canvas-and-layers.md) — placing a picture on the canvas, opacity, blend modes, shadows and filters, text, shape, image and background clips, and matte tracks.
5. [Motion, actions and transitions](motion-and-transitions.md) — actions that animate a clip's properties over time, motion presets, and transitions between clips.
6. [Speed, reverse and freeze frames](speed.md) — constant speed, fitting a clip to a length, rate stretch, speed ramps and their presets, reversing and freeze frames.
7. [Audio](audio.md) — clip levels, fades and their shapes, ducking by clip length or by speech, noise reduction, compression, pan, mute and solo, Normalize and Synchronize Audio.
8. [Remove Silences and Remove Filler Words](cleanup-tools.md) — cutting dead air and filler words out of a spoken recording in one step.
9. [Captions and transcription](captions.md) — importing and exporting captions, and transcribing speech on this Mac or with AssemblyAI into subtitles or word-by-word captions.
10. [Colour grading](color-grading.md) — the Color tab, wheels, curves, looks and LUTs, adjustment clips and qualifiers, Show Ungraded and the scopes.
11. [HDR and colour management](hdr-and-color.md) — how sources are read, camera log, SDR and HDR (HLG) projects, blending, and HDR and SDR deliverables.
12. [Motion graphics](graphics.md) — graphic clips, the built-in graphics, their properties in the inspector, and bringing in your own.
13. [Screen recording](screen-recording.md) — recording a display or a window with system audio, microphone and click rings, recording a camera on its own or beside the screen, and recording voice-overs.
14. [Exporting](export.md) — the export sheet, its formats and settings, presets, the Export Queue, and saving single frames.
15. [The Assistant](assistant.md) — chatting with Claude in the inspector to edit the open project, on your own Anthropic key.
16. [Driving Frame Job from an AI agent (MCP)](mcp.md) — connecting an MCP client such as Claude Code, how calls behave, and every tool.
17. [Settings](settings.md) — the Settings window, updates (Check for Updates… in the downloaded copy), the View choices Frame Job remembers, and where it keeps its files.
18. [Menus and keyboard shortcuts](menus-and-shortcuts.md) — every menu command with its shortcut, and the keys, gestures and context menus that have no menu item.

Writing your own graphic module is covered by the
[graphics API reference](../graphics-api.md).

result.output:
THESIS: Frame Job's edge is a combination no rival has. It is a full editor with broadcast-grade audio, real colour and HDR, and programmable graphics. Every edit is a pure op that can be undone or refused, and the creator, the in-app Assistant and any outside agent all drive the same ops. It runs on the creator's Mac or on the creator's own key, with no credits and no uploads. To lead, Frame Job should ship the jobs that now send creators to Descript, Screen Studio, OpusClip and AutoPod as on-device commands whose results land as ordinary, editable edits on a real timeline: cutting by transcript, cursor-driven screencast polish, vertical reframing, clip finding, speaker switching and camera cutout. An MCP server alone no longer sets a tool apart in 2026; finished creator jobs built from Frame Job's ops do. 

#1 Transcript tab: cut by deleting words, with retakes found for review [L]
  PITCH: A Transcript tab shows the timeline's words in timeline order. The word being spoken is highlighted during playback, and clicking a word moves the playhead to it. Select a sentence and press Delete, and that span ripples out of the video as one undo step. Cut words stay greyed in place and can be restored. A review pass strikes through long pauses and, when an AssemblyAI transcript exists, filler words. After an amending section 11 decision, it also strikes earlier takes of repeated lines and false starts. One click removes everything struck, as one undo step. Words inside nests or transition overlaps show as not editable, with the reason.
  AHEAD: On its own this only brings Frame Job level with Descript, Screen Studio 4, Tella, Loom, Prequel and Gling. Frame Job pulls ahead in four ways. (1) Cost and speed: the on-device transcript costs nothing per minute, while Descript meters media minutes and AI credits and draws complaints about slow scrubbing and exports. (2) No model needed: retakes are found by a deterministic comparison of neighbouring sentences, with no key. (3) Depth: every cut is an ordinary ripple edit in a full editor with the audio chain, grading and graphics behind it, so restoring a cut is exact. (4) Agents: get_transcript already answers in timeline ticks, so 'drop the first take of every repeated line' works the same by click or by chat.
  BUILDS: DeviceTranscriptCache.swift and MediaTranscript.swift (words cached per media), AssemblyAI transcripts, get_transcript (AgentServer+Transcript.swift), rc_project_source_map (speed_map.rs, SR-20), ripple_delete_ranges (core/src/edit_time.rs, one undo step), detect_fillers and its lock, nest and transition rules.
  RISKS: (1) Spec section 11 TR-3, AI-6 and W-9 forbid a pipeline that picks words to cut by meaning. The retake pass needs an amending decision before code. (2) Restore is not one existing op: it is insert_time plus trim_end grouped, or add_clip with a source range. (3) On-device transcription kept 1 of 8 fillers (TR-7), so filler strike-through needs AssemblyAI. (4) MAX_CLIPS 4,096 counts every clip, and each text cut splits every unlocked track, so about 1,000 cuts over 4 tracks hits the cap. (5) The first fill of the view runs the recogniser at a few seconds per minute of speech. (6) Performance on a multi-hour text view is a risk, and the new pane needs a planned file split.

#2 Screen recordings with the cursor as data: auto zoom, cursor polish, keystroke overlays [L]
  PITCH: The recorder stops burning the pointer and click rings into the picture. Beside the movie it saves the cursor's path and image, every click, and, if the creator opts in, the shortcuts pressed. When the recording lands, zoom actions are already on the action lane at each click and each burst of typing. The cursor becomes its own layer: it can be made bigger, restyled, smoothed or hidden when idle, and it gets click ripples. Each shortcut appears as a Keyboard keys overlay, and long typing stretches can be sped up. All of these are ordinary actions, clips and graphics that the creator can drag or delete. Older recordings behave as today.
  AHEAD: The polished-screencast category (Screen Studio, Prequel, Cap, FocuSee, Tella, Camtasia) rests on cursor data. Frame Job's recorder stores none of it, so Frame Job loses its own home segment to a 29-dollar-a-month recorder. This bet brings Frame Job level on polish and ahead on depth: those recorders are shallow editors, while Frame Job's auto zooms are actions on a full timeline next to grading, the audio chain, captions and graphics, and an agent can re-plan them. Free alone is not unique, because OpenScreen is a free MIT-licensed alternative (now archived) and Cap sells a 58-dollar lifetime licence.
  BUILDS: RecordingSetup.swift (it sets showsCursor and showMouseClicks today), add_zoom_action (core/src/edit_zoom.rs), add_speed_ramp, the Keyboard keys graphic template, the recorder panel's grants, recipe_layer.rs, MediaConsolidator and relink.
  RISKS: (1) Spec section 11 recording.md decides three things this bet reverses: the cursor is burned in, callouts stay out, and recordings have no source kind and no schema bump. The owner amends section 11 first. (2) Keystrokes need the Input Monitoring grant, which RecorderStatusItem avoids today. Make it opt-in, record modifier shortcuts only by default, and never record secure fields. (3) The cursor must follow the screen clip's transform and zoom actions, so it is drawn with that clip's layer or nested with it. (4) NSCursor.currentSystem is marked deprecated in macOS 27.0. (5) The sidecar cannot be regenerated, so Consolidate and Relink must carry it. (6) Only new recordings benefit. (7) Timing anchors on the screen's first-frame time (measured within 0.5 ms); issue 370 is a microphone-offset problem and is not inherited.

#3 Make Vertical Version with on-device subject tracking [M (regenerated copy); L for linked versions]
  PITCH: File > Make Vertical Version writes a 9:16 or 1:1 version of a finished 16:9 edit. Each clip fills the frame and follows the face, person or salient region that Vision found on the Mac. It does this with ordinary eased x, y and scale actions the creator can nudge. In a screen recording made after bet 2, it follows the cursor instead. Captions re-lay for the short side, and graphics re-layout from the canvas size. A shot that cannot be cropped gets Add Blurred Background.
  AHEAD: Subject-tracking reframe is table stakes: OpusClip, CapCut, Premiere, Final Cut Pro for iPad, Riverside, Kapwing and Screen Studio all ship it. Auto-repurposing is also the most-wanted creator AI feature in Adobe Express's survey. Frame Job pulls ahead on terms. CapCut moved Auto Reframe behind Pro in April 2026; here it is free and local, and the result is editable pan actions rather than a render. If the owner chooses linked versions (one cut, with framing per shape), Frame Job is ahead of every rival, because their vertical copies drift from the master.
  BUILDS: edit_fit.rs fill_scale, Add Blurred Background (edit_background.rs), word captions sized to the shorter side (CaptionStyle.swift), graphics reading ctx.canvas, actions (edit_action.rs), nests (edit_nest.rs), set_canvas (edit_canvas.rs), File > Duplicate, and the E9 Vision spike in tools/proof/effects_spike/.
  RISKS: (1) Spec section 1 lists auto-reframe as a non-goal, and a section 11 decision must lift it first. Its stated reason, heavy pixel work outside the one-pass compositor, no longer applies, because the output is actions. (2) No two actions on one clip may overlap, of any kind. A clip that already has an action needs a wrapping nest, and a nest's canvas freezes at the size it was nested at. (3) set_canvas does not rescale action end states, so existing zoom actions keep 16:9 targets and must be rewritten. (4) MediaCacheLane is an audio lane, so video analysis needs its own lane, cache kind and ledger rows. (5) Use rectangles and tracking, not masks: the E9 spike found foreground masks flicker. (6) Two-person shots, speakers leaving frame and shot changes inside one clip each need a rule.

#4 Find Clips: ranked moments that open as real vertical edits [M on top of bet 3 (without bet 3 it covers horizontal clips only)]
  PITCH: Clip > Find Clips, run on an episode, VOD or finished edit, lists 10 to 30 candidates of 20 to 60 seconds. Each candidate shows in and out points snapped to sentence ends, its length, a one-line reason (for example 'laughter after the punchline') and a preview. There is no virality score. Make Short turns the checked candidates into vertical projects using bet 3. Each short is word-captioned, has fillers removed where a cloud transcript exists, and is queued for export.
  AHEAD: Long-to-short is the largest paid creator-AI category (OpusClip, Riverside Magic Clips, Submagic, Descript Clips, Kapwing), and all of them meter it by credits. YouTube's own free tool covers only 10 countries and 7 languages. Frame Job pulls ahead in three ways. (1) Local signals: laughter, applause and cheering from Sound Analysis, plus the 10 ms loudness, speech spans and sentence ends, all measured on the Mac. (2) Ranking runs on the creator's own Claude key. (3) Candidates open as editable timelines, not black-box renders. Giving a stated reason instead of a score answers the documented complaint that clippers cut in the wrong place.
  BUILDS: get_transcript (timeline ticks), ClipLoudness.swift and the media loudness cache, media_speech.rs, detect_fillers and ripple_delete_ranges, caption Restyle with Replace, the Export Queue, the Assistant helper (agent/) and its price table, set_range.
  RISKS: (1) Ranking quality is the whole product. (2) On-device FoundationModels has a 4,096-token context and needs Apple Intelligence, so it is a chunked, weaker fallback rather than an equal path. (3) Speaker labels exist only on AssemblyAI transcripts requested with speakers. (4) No op copies a timeline range into a new project (new_project takes a path; Duplicate copies everything), so one is needed. (5) Sound Analysis labels are noisy on game audio and music beds. (6) Long transcripts cost tokens, so show an estimate range first.

#5 Switch by Speaker, and read every audio track of a file [M (stacked-track switching plus every audio track); L for a multicam clip with an angle grid]
  PITCH: Bring two to four cameras and a mic per person and line them up with Synchronize Audio, then choose Clip > Switch by Speaker. Frame Job cuts to whoever is talking, judging each mic's speech spans against that mic's own noise floor. It uses the wide shot during crosstalk and holds a minimum shot length. The whole switch is one undo step, and every cut is an ordinary split the creator can roll or re-pick. OBS multitrack files and multichannel recorder files now import every audio track, not only the first.
  AHEAD: Automatic switching is sold as AutoPod (about 29 dollars a month), as Resolve SmartSwitch (in Studio) and inside metered or hand-off tools (Descript, Eddie). Premiere users have asked for it for years. Video podcasts are the fastest-growing creator format. Frame Job already owns the hard audio half: drift-corrected sync, cached speech spans, the loudness cache, Match Audio, Enhance Voice, the leveller, a -16 LUFS target and stems. It can add the picture half for free, and an agent can re-run the switch with new rules.
  BUILDS: AudioSync*.swift (alignment as move_clip and set_speed), SileroVAD.swift and media_speech.rs, audio_duck_speech.rs, ClipLoudness.swift, set_enabled (a disabled clip is not decoded, per nest.rs shows_video), ProjectDocument.performGroupedEdit, core/src/container.rs and every CompositionBuilder.firstTrack audio caller.
  RISKS: (1) Spec section 1 lists multicam as a non-goal, so a section 11 decision must lift it, narrowly or fully. (2) Reading every audio track touches every firstTrack(.audio) caller (the builder, Silence, the isolation, ramp, voice and reverse renderers, and the transcription extract) and needs a format bump. (3) Splitting linked picture and sound halves of 3 angles every 8 s for 2 h gives about 5,400 clips, over the 4,096 cap. Cut picture only and keep the mics whole. (4) Mic bleed can mislead the switch, and one-mic shows need Vision mouth activity. (5) Decoding 3 to 4 angles of 4K is unmeasured. (6) Zoom and Riverside already deliver one file per participant, so the multitrack fix chiefly serves OBS and multichannel WAV.

#6 Camera cutout without a green screen, and camera layouts [L]
  PITCH: Tick Remove Background on a camera clip. Vision segments the person on the Mac, rendered in the background the way Reverse is. A Layout pop-up switches the camera at the playhead, with an animated move, between corner bubble (circle or rounded), side by side, stacked for vertical, camera full and screen only. 'Hide camera while silent' fades the camera out during pauses. Text Behind Subject follows from cutout: a title sits between the person and their background.
  AHEAD: This is mostly catch-up. Screen Studio 4 (cutout in beta), Cap 0.6, Tella, Prequel and Loom shipped camera cutout or layouts in September and October 2026, and Final Cut Pro, Premiere and Resolve ship one-click subject masks. Frame Job's recorded camera is fixed in the bottom-right corner. Frame Job pulls ahead only in combination: layouts are actions any agent can write, the camera gets Frame Job's grading and LUT engine, and with bet 2 the whole screencast polish lives inside a full editor.
  BUILDS: Issue 124 and its E9 Vision spike, ReverseRenderer and ReverseCache with BackgroundRender and MediaCacheLedger, matte tracks (recipe_matte.rs), actions over transform, crop, corner radius and shadow, Add Background, speech spans of the microphone media.
  RISKS: (1) Hair and edge quality is a risk. Balanced masks are 512x384 and likely need a refinement pass. Accurate masks run at 1.7x realtime and take 1.7 GiB per minute. (2) Non-person masks flicker on video, so non-person cutout is for stills only. (3) A mask on a Luma matte track has no link to the camera clip and drifts on trims, splits and speed changes, so a per-layer mask with a format bump is the sound design. (4) Issue 124's texture(2) binding is stale: looks hold texture 2 and curves texture 3. (5) The camera clip has no sound, so hide-while-silent reads the microphone's spans. (6) Spec section 1's ML non-goal and issue 124's D5 must enter section 11 first. (7) The 8-decoder warning applies, and HLG needs the mask in the right working space.

ALSO:
 - Proposals: play an agent's multi-step edit before it lands | M (Proposals), then M (Recipes) | Only Frame Job can do this. Its handles are immutable, it can render a project that is not the current one (the export pin does), and it can group edits into one undo step (performGroupedEdit). An agent's whole turn becomes a side chain that the creator plays, compares A/B with the current cut, and then accepts as one named step or rejects. Adobe's 2026 survey found 44% of creators who want more agent independence want to review, edit or undo, and 37% want to see what the agent is doing. This am
 - Punch in on cuts | S | The standard fix for the jump cuts that bet 1, Remove Silences and filler removal leave behind. It alternates scale between about 100% and 112% across cuts within one take, centred on the face, using set_video x, y and scale as one grouped step. It is free and exact, and it needs no disclosure. Ship it alone, right after bet 1's first phase.
 - Source ranges, skimming, In and Out, favourite ranges | M | Today a placed clip is always the whole file. Letting add_clip, insert_clip and overwrite_clip take a source range is an op-table change that opTool prints into the MCP tools automatically. It is also the precondition for placing a found moment or a search hit, and for restoring a transcript cut cleanly. Add proxies only after a measurement shows a shortfall, and only under a recorded decision on a playback-only builder input.
 - Caption styles, brand kit and project templates | M | Repeat creators redo the same caption looks, intros and lower thirds every episode, and Frame Job has four hard-coded text presets with no saved styles. Colour controls are safe under W-10. Size and font changes need re-paging or a W-10 amendment. Per-word emphasis and emoji need a model_words.rs field and a format bump under W-2 and W-3, and whether emoji render correctly in HLG projects is unverified.
 - Publish polish slice | S | Three cheap items. (1) A copyable 00:00 chapter list from chapter markers, checked against YouTube's rule (at least 3 chapters, the first at 00:00, each at least 10 s), which otherwise fails silently. (2) Approximate platform safe-zone overlays. (3) Named platform export targets. Skip AI titles and thumbnails, because YouTube Studio already offers them free.
 - Measure multi-stream 4K and multi-hour playback | S | Playback is checked at 60 fps on a 1080p movie only (PB-2), plus a few 4K rows. Bet 5 at 3 to 4 angles and any claim to be a 'leading' editor depend on this figure. It is a measurement, not performance work, so it fits the owner's features-first order.
 - search_media over cached transcripts | S | The cheap, useful slice of the on-device footage index: one agent and Media-tab search across every media item's cached words. Build Vision and Sound Analysis analysis inside the features that use it (bets 3, 4 and 6), not as a standalone index.
 - Merge the in-app tutorials after the owner's trial | S | Tutorials TU0 to TU3 sit on an unmerged branch, and the owner's TU4 trial is still owed. Creators arriving from CapCut need onboarding. The merge needs TutorialTargets rows for the audio road map.
 - Optical-flow slow motion, spike first | S spike, then M | VTFrameProcessor frame-rate conversion runs offline in the existing Reverse pipeline. On this Mac it accepts only 64RGBAHalf, and how it handles HDR encodings is untested. Lifting the spec section 1 non-goal waits for the spike. Interpolated smooth cuts across a jump cut stay a spike, not a commitment.
 - WebVTT import; translated captions later | S (import), M (translation) | WebVTT import is a small CaptionImporter addition. On-device translated captions and soft subtitle tracks can be a later phase of a caption road map. Platforms already translate for free, so they do not merit a bet of their own.
NOT:
 - Generative media: AI B-roll and video, avatars and AI twins, voice cloning, lip-synced dubbing | Nothing on the device can do it, so it would mean brokering credit-metered vendor APIs across several keys whose models change constantly. That is the business model Frame Job competes against. It also carries disclosure and authenticity risk under YouTube's synthetic-content rule. YouTube already dubs in 27 languages for all creators, and Instagram translates with lip sync free in 14.
 - Direct upload, scheduling, hosted share links, platform analytics | An open-source app with no backend cannot keep OAuth client secrets. A shared YouTube quota would cap all users together, and TikTok and Meta posting APIs need audits. Share links need a server, and the platforms own the analytics. Export per platform and copy the chapter text instead. Share links could come later only as bring-your-own storage.
 - Stock music, SFX and B-roll libraries; a template marketplace | These need licensing, curation, bandwidth and a backend. One developer cannot match CapCut's template volume or Apple building MotionVFX into Final Cut Pro. The counter already exists: agent-written graphics and shareable .fjgraphic packages.
 - Eye-contact correction and face retouching | Apple has no public API for gaze or face reshaping in recorded video. It would need cloud or custom generative face models with uncanny failures, likeness risk and a per-frame cost that the one-pass compositor cannot absorb. None of the six creator workflows breaks here.
 - Cloud sync, real-time collaboration, mobile or iPad apps, Windows | Each needs a backend or a second platform, and each is off the local, open, Mac-only position.
 - Remote guest recording and live multi-camera capture | That is Riverside's moat, and it needs WebRTC servers. Import the per-guest files that Riverside, Zoom and StreamYard already produce, and switch between them with bet 5.
 - A virality score on found clips | Reviewers distrust auto-clip scores and discard many scored clips. A stated reason per moment is honest and something the creator can control.
 - An on-device footage index as a standalone headline | Final Cut Pro, Resolve and Premiere all shipped footage search within a year, so it is no longer distinctive. Vision gives only fixed-taxonomy labels, so free-text search needs a bundled model whose licence is unverified. The talking-head and screencast creator rarely has a large library. Build the slices inside bets 3, 4 and 6, plus a transcript search tool.
 - Script to cut: a listening teleprompter that assembles takes | Teleprompters are commoditised: Descript and Tella have them, and free notch teleprompters with voice tracking exist. Script-first recording suits a minority of creators. SpeechEngine.swift is file-based today, and judging fillers needs the cloud. The valuable kernel, best-take and retake removal, belongs in bet 1.
 - Translated captions and soft subtitle tracks as a bet | The pilot figure that more than 25% of watch time comes from other languages measured dubbed audio, not subtitles. Platforms translate captions themselves. ADA Title II requires same-language captions, which Frame Job already makes. YouTube, Vimeo and LMSs take sidecar SRT or VTT files, which Frame Job already writes. It fits as a later phase, not as a bet.
 - A publish kit as a headline, especially AI titles, descriptions and thumbnails | YouTube Studio offers AI title suggestions and title and thumbnail tests for free. The on-device model's roughly 4k-token context cannot hold a long transcript. Frame Job already meets the loudness targets. Only the S-sized slice is worth doing.
 - More MCP surface or a second agent mode as the headline | In 2026 Descript, Kapwing, OpusClip, Submagic, VEED, Riverside and Resolve all have MCP servers. Every creator job shipped as ops becomes an agent tool anyway. Proposals stay in the next tier as the trust feature, not the headline.
 - Stabilisation, for now | Phones stabilise in camera, and stabilisation mainly serves handheld vlogs rather than the talking-head, screencast and podcast segments where Frame Job can lead. It is feasible later as a Vision registration rendered to a cached copy.
 - Live-compositor motion blur | Blur on animated layers needs several sub-frame passes, which breaks the one-pass compositor. At most it could become export-only accumulation later.
 - A plugin system: third-party effects, user shaders, Audio Unit hosting | It contradicts the closed, versioned effect vocabulary (spec section 11 R5-1, G-1) behind preview and export parity and the proof suite. That vocabulary is what makes agent editing trustworthy. JS graphic modules stay the one extension point.
 - Pro finishing as headline features: Dolby Vision, synthetic depth of field | Resolve and Final Cut Pro own these. They cost compositor work, and the owner has already closed several colour items. Frame Job's colour and HDR already lead every creator tool.
 - Analytics-driven idea and trend features | The platforms hold the performance data (the Edits assistant, YouTube tests), and these features do not use the local, agent-driven editor advantage.
DECISIONS:
 - Which creator segment to lead with. Recommendation: creators who record themselves talking, meaning talking-head YouTube and screen tutorials (bets 1, 2 and 6). Then repurposing to shorts (bets 3 and 4), then video podcasts (bet 5).
 - Which spec section 1 non-goals to lift, and in what scope. Auto-reframe is needed for bet 3. Multicam can be lifted narrowly, as speaker switching on stacked tracks, or fully, as a multicam clip with an angle grid (bet 5). ML and heavy pixel work are needed for camera cutout (issue 124's D5, bet 6). Optical-flow retiming and motion blur stay out until a spike. A plugin system stays out.
 - Which spec section 11 decisions to amend before code: TR-3, AI-6 and W-9, so that a deterministic retake pass may strike words (bet 1); recording.md (cursor as data, callouts, a source kind and schema bump; bet 2); AI-10 (Proposals); W-10 (inspector caption styling).
 - Whether the recorder may ask for the Input Monitoring grant to capture shortcuts, opt-in and modifier keys only by default.
 - Vertical versions: a regenerated copy (M) or linked versions in one project, where one cut has a framing per shape (L, with a format bump).
 - Language models: Claude on the creator's key only, or Apple FoundationModels as a no-key fallback for ranking and drafts. FoundationModels needs Apple Intelligence on and has a context of about 4k tokens.
 - Cloud: confirm that bring-your-own-key stays the only cloud model. Then either accept that filler detection stays AssemblyAI-only (TR-7), or fund an on-device filler pass.
 - Performance: allow one measurement of multi-stream 4K and multi-hour playback now, despite the features-first order, before bet 5 and before any claim to lead. Add proxies only if the measurement falls short.
 - Real use: cut at least one real video per lead segment in Frame Job before or alongside the first bet, so the bets are tested against real work.
 - Positioning: whether to present Frame Job to creators as free, open, on-device and credit-free. That position answers the most common switching triggers: price rises, metered credits and content-licence scares.

# Creator survey: what would make Frame Job a leading creator editor

## Summary

This survey is dated 1 November 2026. It asks what would make Frame Job a leading editor for content creators. It draws on five inputs:

- an inventory of the tree;
- four research sweeps (creator tools, pro editors, screen and tutorial tools, creator demand);
- three strategists' proposals;
- the candidates merged from those proposals;
- adversarial checks of each candidate against the code, Apple's frameworks and the market.

content.text:
Adding more general features won't do it. Frame Job already has more depth than any creator-first tool: the audio chain, grading and HDR, programmable graphics, and every edit open to an agent.

What would put it ahead is doing the specific jobs that currently send creators to Descript, Screen Studio, OpusClip and AutoPod. Each would run on the Mac with no credits or uploads, and each would land as ordinary edits you can change on a real timeline. Being agent-driven isn't a differentiator on its own any more: Descript, Kapwing, OpusClip, VEED, Riverside and Resolve all have MCP servers now. Finished creator jobs built from Frame Job's edits would be.

## The six bets, ranked

1. **Edit by transcript (L).** A Transcript tab where you delete words to cut the video, and cut words stay greyed so you can restore them. A review pass marks pauses, fillers and repeated takes, and one click removes them all. Today Frame Job has the words, `get_transcript` and multi-range ripple delete, but no text editor. This is Descript's core feature, and here it's free and on-device. The retake pass needs an amended §11 decision (TR-3, AI-6, W-9).
2. **Recordings that keep the cursor as data (L).** This is the biggest gap in Frame Job's own home segment. The recorder currently burns the pointer and click rings into the picture (`RecordingSetup.swift:223`), so it can't do what Screen Studio does. Recording the cursor's path, the clicks and (opt-in) shortcuts makes these possible:
   - automatic zoom actions at each click and burst of typing;
   - a cursor you can enlarge, smooth or hide;
   - click ripples;
   - keyboard-shortcut overlays.

   It reverses three decisions in §11's recording file, and capturing shortcuts needs the Input Monitoring permission.
3. **Make Vertical Version (M, or L for linked versions).** Turns a 16:9 edit into 9:16 or 1:1, following the face or subject with Vision on the Mac. The result is ordinary pan and zoom actions you can nudge, not a render. Every rival has this, and CapCut moved it behind its paid tier in April 2026. It requires lifting the auto-reframe non-goal.
4. **Find Clips (M, on top of bet 3).** Finds the best 20–60 s moments in an episode or stream using on-device signals and ranks them on your own Claude key. Each comes with a stated reason rather than a "virality score", and Make Short opens it as an editable, captioned vertical project. Clip-finding is the largest paid creator-AI category, and every rival charges per use.
5. **Switch by Speaker (M).** Once cameras and mics are lined up with Synchronize Audio, Frame Job cuts to whoever is talking, as ordinary edits you can adjust. It also imports every audio track of OBS and multichannel files; today only the first is read. Frame Job already has the hard audio half of this. It requires lifting multicam at least narrowly.
6. **Camera cutout and layouts (L).** On-device background removal for the camera, plus layouts you switch at the playhead: corner bubble, side by side, stacked, full. Today the recorded camera is fixed in the bottom-right corner. This is mostly catching up, since Screen Studio 4, Cap, Tella and Loom shipped it in September and October 2026. Issue #124 is its starting point.

**Next tier:**
- Preview an agent's multi-step edit as one step you accept or reject. Only Frame Job's design makes this possible.
- Punch-in zooms on jump cuts.
- Clips that use only part of a source file: today `add_clip` always places the whole file.
- Caption styles, brand kits and templates.
- A YouTube chapter list you can copy, plus platform safe zones.
- Search across cached transcripts.
- Merge the tutorials branch.
- Measure several 4K streams and multi-hour playback before any claim to lead.

**Not worth chasing:**
- AI video, avatars, voice cloning and dubbing.
- Direct upload and share links: these need a backend, and an open-source app can't keep the platforms' sign-in secrets.
- Stock libraries and a template marketplace.
- Eye-contact correction: Apple offers no API for it.
- Collaboration or sync.
- A plugin system.
- Stabilisation and motion blur, for now.

## Decisions only you can make

- **Which creators to lead with.** The recommendation is people who record themselves talking: talking-head YouTube and screen tutorials (bets 1, 2, 6). Then repurposing to shorts (3, 4), then video podcasts (5).
- **Which non-goals to lift:** auto-reframe, multicam (narrow or full), and on-device ML for cutout. Optical-flow retiming and motion blur would wait for a spike; plugins stay out.
- **Whether the recorder may ask for Input Monitoring** to capture shortcuts.
- **Whether bring-your-own-key stays the only cloud model.** Apple's on-device FoundationModels could be a no-key fallback, but its context is only about 4k tokens.
- **Cutting one real video per lead segment** in Frame Job alongside the first bet, so the bets are tested against real work.

The full survey, with the market by segment, each bet's risks and every source, is in `designs/creator-survey.md`. It isn't committed. I checked the code claims above against the tree; the market claims carry their sources in that file but I haven't independently re-checked them.

# Road map "audio" — a professional audio toolset (tiers A and B)

**Opened 2026-10-30** (AP0), when the owner answered the five choices below ("Yes, lift scopes,
and allow Apple's built-in audio effects", then "OK" to each of the rest): AU-2…AU-4, and spec
§1's audio non-goal lifted. The brief
is `designs/audio-survey.md` (its tiers A and B; tier C is not in this road map). The worktree is
`.claude/worktrees/audio-updates`, branch `worktree-audio-updates`, from `33eeed0`. Decisions are
AU-2 onward, in `designs/spec/11-decisions/audio.md` (AU-1, the ×32 volume ceiling, is built).

## Goal

Frame Job's audio today is a creator-tier strip: volume, fades, clip-extent ducking, pan, mono,
a compressor, steady-noise reduction, peak Normalize, and an export loudness target that only
turns the mix down (`docs/guide/audio.md`, `docs/guide/export.md`). After this road map a person
can take a quiet, noisy or uneven voice recording to a delivery loudness with one command and
then refine it: loudness they can see and target, a true-peak limiter, EQ, a gate, a de-esser,
hum removal, voice isolation, parameters that move over time, J- and L-cuts, track faders and
buses, stems, speech-aware ducking, matching, scrubbing and voice effects. Every control has its
MCP mirror, as every control does today.

## What it delivers first

The owner's recording, `samples/Rode-usb-mic.m4a`, peaks at −18.6 dBFS with an integrated
loudness of −44.7 LUFS. Peak Normalize and the export's loudness target both stop near −27 LUFS
(the survey's §2), because neither can reduce a peak. **After AP2, one Normalize press in
Loudness mode takes it to the chosen target (−16 LUFS by default) at −1 dBTP.** After AP6, one
Enhance Voice press also cleans it: the high-pass, the noise floor in the pauses (about
−36 dBFS once lifted, 65 % of the file), the compressor set from the clip's own level, the
limiter and the target.

## The owner's choices (answered 2026-10-30: all five as recommended)

Recorded as AU-2 (choice 1), AU-3 (choices 4 and 5) and AU-4 (choices 2 and 3). The owner,
on the rest: "We'll address other questions as we progress. If builds can be run in multiple
lanes, do so."

1. **Scope (spec §1).** Lift "no EQ" and "no mix buses", and allow Apple's own audio units
   inside Frame Job (as `AVAudioUnitTimePitch` already runs for speed-ramp audio). Hosting
   third-party Audio Unit plug-ins stays out of this road map (tier C, C5). *Recommended.*
2. **Normalize's default.** Keep peak normalize as the button's default until AP2's limiter
   lands, then make **Loudness** the default with Peak a choice beside it. *Recommended.*
3. **The default loudness target.** −16 LUFS integrated at −1 dBTP (voice platforms and
   podcasts), with −14 (YouTube's playback reference) and −23 (EBU R 128) as quick picks.
   *Recommended.*
4. **Own DSP or Apple's units for the live stages.** Frame Job's own DSP for EQ, gate,
   de-esser, hum notch and limiter, written beside the compressor: live in the tap,

- **The clip strip runs in a tap, before the fader.** `AudioTap.swift` (595) puts one
  `MTAudioProcessingTap` (PreEffects) on each composition audio track and schedules each clip's

  recorded level**, so a level-relative stage (limiter, gate) must be told the clip's gain.
- **The preview has no post-mix insert; the export does.** One tap per input, already used by
  the meter (`LevelMeter.swift` 400, which sums per-track peaks as an upper bound, not the mix).

## Goal

Frame Job finishes video better than most creator tools: its audio chain, colour and HDR, codecs and
an MCP surface over the whole editor (survey, "What Frame Job has"). It loses creators earlier, at
six jobs that now define a creator editor. After this road map each is a command that runs on the
Mac, lands as ordinary undo steps on a real timeline, and has an MCP tool that runs the same
planner:

1. **The Transcript tab (TX).** The timeline read as words, in timeline order. Selected words are
   deleted on every unlocked track as one step; cut words stay greyed and come back with Restore
   Words. A review pass strikes long pauses, fillers (where an AssemblyAI transcript exists),
   retakes, restarts and repeats, for the person to keep or remove in one step.
2. **Screen recordings with the cursor as data (CU).** The recorder saves the cursor's path, images,
   clicks, scrolls and (opt-in) shortcuts beside the movie, and the editor draws the cursor as part
   of the screen clip's layer. Auto Zoom, shortcut overlays, sped-up typing and motion blur follow,
   each as ordinary actions and clips, and the recorder can run them on landing.
3. **Make Vertical Version (VR).** A 9:16 or 1:1 copy of a finished edit, each picture following the
   face, person or salient region Vision found on the Mac (the cursor in a recording made after CU,
   the speaker in a two-shot after SW), as eased x, y and scale actions; captions re-paged and
   graphics re-laid. Linked versions in one project are designed and asked.
4. **Find Clips (FC).** A long recording analysed on the Mac (sentences, speakers, loudness,
   laughter, applause, cheering), ranked by Claude on the person's key with a stated reason per
   moment and no score, and made into saved, captioned, vertical shorts on the Export Queue.
5. **Switch by Speaker, and every audio track (SW).** A program track of shots cut to whoever is
   speaking, judged on each microphone against its own level; Switch Angle; an Angle Viewer and
   switching while playing; a one-microphone mode from faces. Every audio track and channel of a
   file played, measured and transcribed.
6. **Camera cutout and layouts (CO).** Remove Background on a camera clip from Vision's person
   masks, Text Behind Subject, camera layouts switched at the playhead (corner, side by side,
   stacked, camera full, screen only), the same at record time, and the camera hidden while silent.

The shared phases (CJ) give a person two things directly — every command that would send to Claude
or AssemblyAI greyed without its key, with a tooltip saying which key and where; and Clip ▸ Split at
Shot Changes and File ▸ New Project from Range… — and give the bets one key gate, one analysis lane,
store, reader and sheet, a decided clip ceiling, and the files at the cap cut once before three
lanes reach for them.

## What it delivers first

The lead segment is people who record themselves talking: talking-head YouTube and screen tutorials
(TX, CU, CO). Repurposing to shorts comes next (VR, FC), then video podcasts (SW).

- **The baseline.** When TX1 starts, the owner cuts T1 (a talking head, sample S-TH1) and T2 (a
  screen tutorial, S-ST1) in that day's build, to a state they would publish, and records every
  point where they left Frame Job or gave up (CJ-5).
- **The checkpoint, after TX3.** The owner reads T1 as text in the Transcript tab, follows it while
  it plays, clicks a word to seek, selects words and presses ⌫ to cut them on every unlocked track
  as one step "Delete Words". They cut T1 again this way; the verdict is recorded before TX4 starts,
  and lane A builds CJ5a meanwhile.

The full design is written to `designs/creator-jobs.md`. Your answers and how I applied them are in its "The owner's answers" section, and everything needed to begin after compaction is saved.

**Scale:** it's 6,538 lines and 91 phases, about four and a half times the audio road map. It has 10 provisional format bumps, or 11 if linked vertical versions are built.

**How it was checked:** seven designers each had an adversary check their section against the code, the §11 decisions and Apple's documentation, and then revised. One agent merged the sections. A completeness critic and a code-claim checker then found 1 blocker and 21 should-fix problems. The blocker was speaker-switching phases depending on files that other lanes create. The should-fix problems included wrong line ranges for file splits and menu items placed in the wrong file. A final pass fixed all 22. That pass's own edits weren't reviewed again; each phase's pipeline re-reads the code before building, which should catch what's left.

**Three lanes:**
- **A, words:** the key gate, the Transcript tab, then Find Clips, then every audio track.
- **B, recorder:** the cursor recorded as data, Auto Zoom, shortcut overlays, sped-up typing, motion blur. Then camera layouts, which also come at record time, and hiding the camera while silent.
- **C, pictures:** a shared video-analysis cache, camera cutout and Text Behind Subject. Then Make Vertical Version, then Switch by Speaker, the Angle Viewer and switching while playing.

**Your trials:**
- When TX1 starts, you cut a talking-head video (T1) and a screen tutorial (T2) in that day's build. These are the baseline.
- After TX3, you cut T1 again by deleting words. Your verdict is recorded before TX4 starts.
- TX8 is the closing run.
- Screen-tutorial, shorts and podcast trials come later in their own bets.

**Samples you'll record (21 in all):**
- First, at TX1:
  - **S-TH1:** a GH5 talking head, with the RØDE recorded beside it.
  - **S-ST1:** a screen tutorial with the camera, made with today's recorder.
  - **S-RT1:** a retake script read on the RØDE.
- Later: two-person podcast setups, a green-cloth clip, OBS multitrack files, a laughter and applause take, and an hour-long recording. The road map's "Samples the owner supplies" lists each one, the phase that first needs it, and what it measures.

CJ0a, the first phase, asks you eight questions before any code. Answer them now and they'll survive the compaction; a reply of "all as recommended" works.

1. Merge into main after each phase lands, or once at the close? *Recommended: after each phase.*
2. Also lift spec §2's "Left out" list (pointer effects, templates, publishing to YouTube or Vimeo, stock media)? This makes them allowed, not built. *Recommended: yes.*
3. Keep your samples in `tools/proof/media/creator/`, which is gitignored and never committed? *Recommended: yes.*
4. Measure playback of 3–4 synced 4K angles and multi-hour files before building Switch by Speaker? This needs about 34 GB of test files. *Recommended: yes, as SW0.*

You are the orchestrator. You do almost no work yourself. You dispatch one subagent at a time, in a fixed order, and check stop conditions between stages. Never spawn two agents at once. Never spawn an agent not listed below. Never explore the codebase yourself — that is the designer's job.

1. Derive `<repo-name>` from the git remote or the directory name, and `<task-slug>` from the request (kebab-case, ≤6 words, append `-2`, `-3` if it exists).
2. `HANDOFF=~/.claude/litecode/<repo-name>/<task-slug>/`. Create it. Write the user's verbatim request to `$HANDOFF/request.md`.

Every dispatch prompt has the same shape: one or two lines telling the agent the `$HANDOFF` path and which files to read. Dispatches to agents that write from a template also give the `$TEMPLATES` path. Do not paste file contents into the prompt; the agent reads them.

## Pipeline

### Stage 0 — triage (`lc-triage`) — always runs

Dispatch: `Handoff dir: $HANDOFF. Read request.md. Write 00-triage.md.`

Read `00-triage.md`. If `route: small` → go to Stage 3. If `route: full` → Stage 1.

### Stage 1 — design (`lc-designer`)

Dispatch: `Handoff dir: $HANDOFF. Templates dir: $TEMPLATES. Read request.md and 00-triage.md. Explore the repo as needed. Write 01-spec.md using the spec template.`

### Stage 2 — adversary (`lc-adversary`)

Dispatch: `Handoff dir: $HANDOFF. Templates dir: $TEMPLATES. Read 01-spec.md and only the files it names. Write 02-objections.md.`

Read the verdict line. If `verdict: proceed` and there are zero objections, copy `01-spec.md` to `03-spec-final.md` and go to Stage 3.

### Stage 1b — final design (`lc-designer`)

Dispatch: `Handoff dir: $HANDOFF. Templates dir: $TEMPLATES. Read 01-spec.md and 02-objections.md. Write 03-spec-final.md: the revised spec plus an "Objections addressed" section.`

### Stage 3 — implement (`lc-implementer`)

Full route dispatch: `Handoff dir: $HANDOFF. Read 03-spec-final.md. Implement it. Write 04-impl-notes.md and 04-checks.txt.`

Small route dispatch: `Handoff dir: $HANDOFF. Read request.md and 00-triage.md. No spec exists; implement the request directly, touching only files_likely_touched unless you justify otherwise in your notes. Write 04-impl-notes.md and 04-checks.txt.`

Check for `STOP:` in the notes. If present, halt.

### Stage 4 — review (`lc-reviewer`)

**Skip check first.** Run `git diff --stat` (or the equivalent for the repo's VCS). If total changed lines < 80 AND `04-checks.txt` shows every verification command passing (a command recorded as `SKIPPED:` with a reason counts as passing) → skip to **Finish**.

Otherwise dispatch: `Handoff dir: $HANDOFF. Templates dir: $TEMPLATES. Read 03-spec-final.md (or request.md on the small route), 04-impl-notes.md, 04-checks.txt, and the git diff. Write 05-review.md.`

If `verdict: pass` → **Finish**. If `verdict: fix-required` → Stage 5.

### Stage 5 — fix loop (`lc-fixer`, then `lc-reviewer`), at most 5 passes

Fix pass `N` runs from 1 to 5. The review it answers is `05-review.md` for pass 1, and `07-review-N.md` (the re-review written after pass `N-1`) after that.

1. Fix dispatch: `Handoff dir: $HANDOFF. Read <that review> and the git diff. Fix every blocker and should-fix. Re-run the spec's verification commands that your fixes can affect. Write 06-fix-notes-N.md.`
2. If the fix notes contain `STOP:`, halt (see **Stopping**).
3. Re-review dispatch: `Handoff dir: $HANDOFF. Templates dir: $TEMPLATES. Read 03-spec-final.md (or request.md on the small route), 04-impl-notes.md, 04-checks.txt, every 06-fix-notes-*.md so far, the review pass N answered, and the git diff. Write 07-review-<N+1>.md.`
4. If that review says `verdict: pass` → **Finish**. If it says `fix-required` and `N < 5` → run pass `N+1`. If `N = 5` → do NOT run the fixer again. Go to **Finish** and report the unresolved findings.

**Stop early** if a re-review lists a blocker or should-fix that the previous review also raised (the same finding at the same file:line) and the fix notes claim it fixed. Go to **Finish** and report that finding as stuck. A sixth pass won't fix what two passes couldn't.

## Stopping

Any stage may write `STOP: <reason>` at the top of its output file. When you see it: halt, tell the user the reason, list the handoff files that exist, and ask how to proceed. Do not try to work around it yourself.

## Resume

List `$HANDOFF`. Restart from the first stage whose output file is missing, following the same routing rules. If `00-triage.md` says `small`, the missing spec files are expected — go by the small route. In the fix loop, the pass number is one more than the count of `06-fix-notes-*.md` already written. If the newest file is a fix note with no `07-review-*.md` after it, run that pass's re-review first. A handoff dir from before the loop (`06-fix-notes.md`, `07-review-2.md`) counts as pass 1.

## Finish

Print a summary, in this order, nothing extra:

- Route: small / full
- Stages run (including how many fix passes)
- Files changed (from `git diff --stat`)
- Verification: pass / fail, with the failing command names if any
- Objections the designer declined (from `03-spec-final.md`), one line each, if any
- Unresolved review findings (blockers / should-fix), if any
- Handoff dir path

## Rules you must not break

- One agent at a time. Sequential only.
- No agent outside the six defined. No ad-hoc "let me just check" subagents.
- Never skip triage.
- Never run more than 5 fix passes, and never run a fix pass without a `fix-required` review in front of it.
- Never paste handoff file contents into dispatch prompts — pass paths.
- You do not read source files. If you're tempted to, you're doing the designer's job at the wrong effort level.

content.text:
Every question is answered, and the answers are committed in the road map as `eb350b86`. All of them took the recommendation except SW0, which will also generate a synthetic three-hour test file now. Main is fast-forwarded and nothing is pushed.

**Round 2 landed (5 phases):**
- **CJ5a:** the core op that copies a timeline range into a whole project. It filed #427, an edge case where a split can leave a piece too short for its transition.
- **CU0a:** the recorder's decisions and its five file splits.
- **CU0b:** the cursor spikes. Only the file-size test could run, and it passed: a cursor file of about 10 MB parses in 14 ms. The click, keyboard and display spikes couldn't run because the console was locked.
- **CU1a:** the cursor file format, read and checked by the core. Its proof scored 7/7 against Release.
- **CJ2a:** the shared video-analysis cache and on-device shot detection, with a `get_media_analysis` tool for agents. Its proof scored 22/22 against Release, and it filed #428 and #429.

**Two things need you at the machine, unlocked:**

# The cursor spikes — road map "creator-jobs", CU0b

What the road map measures before any cursor code is written:
- **CU-S1:** the capture APIs, the grants, the event clock and the cursor's image.
- **CU-S2:** the mapping from global points to movie pixels, and the time anchor.
- **CU-S3:** whether ScreenCaptureKit's dirty rects locate typing.
- **CU-S4:** the cursor file's size and speed, measured on a reader prototype.

**The answers are not here.** They are in `designs/creator-jobs.md`'s "CU0b's record" (the VERDICT lines and the rows) and in spec §11 CU-6's "Settled at CU0b" line. Each rule is the road map's own entry under "Every spike, with its rule", fixed at CJ0a. R0 hashes each entry by CJ-7's definition: the line `- **<ID> —` and every following line that begins with two spaces. It compares the hash with CJ0a's pinned value (`deciders.PINNED`) and refuses to run a changed rule (`RULE CHANGED <id>`, exit 1, nothing written). Each `results.json` stores its value as `rule_sha256`. What is here is how to run them again.

```sh
python3 tools/proof/cursor_spike/cursor_spike.py --selftest                     # R0, S1a–S4a, T1, R4a; builds only the reader
python3 tools/proof/cursor_spike/cursor_spike.py --selftest --mutant body-or    # each of the ten must exit 1
python3 tools/proof/cursor_spike/cursor_spike.py --build-only                   # R0 and B0
python3 tools/proof/cursor_spike/cursor_spike.py --only s4                      # one group; each fits 600 s
python3 tools/proof/cursor_spike/cursor_spike.py --only s1,s2,s3                # the auto and posted tiers
python3 tools/proof/cursor_spike/cursor_spike.py --only s1,s2 --person          # the person tier (JOB-29), merged in
```

The mutants are `rule-unchecked`, `clicks-95`, `keys-accessibility-ok`, `grant-iohid-first`, `skipped-as-measured`, `inherited-grant-counted`, `caret-unflipped`, `odd-window-ignored`, `dirty-128` and `body-or`. Each is switched in-process through `deciders.MUTANT`.

**The runs touch the machine.** They warp the pointer (restoring it after each row), show full-screen grey windows above everything (`.statusBar + 1`), open small helper windows, and set the instrument's own cursor. Keep your hands off the mouse and keyboard, except where the person tier asks for them. Frame Job itself is never launched.

**Exit codes.**
- **0:** every requested row was answered or skipped by name, whatever the verdict.
- **1:** an instrument failure. That is B0 (a build, the bundle's codesign or the reader), a probe crash or expiry, a still frame with fewer red pixels than half the crosshair's (or Separate's marker's) expected count, R4a's bodies disagreeing, a selftest row (so a mutant caught under `--mutant` exits 1), or `RULE CHANGED`.
- **2:** not performed: `core/target/release/libframejob_core.a` or `build/codecs/stamp.json` is missing (`swift_build.build` links both).

A skipped row is never a failure. A row skipped before its field's value is settled makes that field `owed`. A row the rule makes conditional and the host lacks, such as a second display, is `absent`, which is not a skip.

## The tiers

- **auto:**
  - A4: the poll's cost over 10,000 calls, and ten warps read back.
  - A5: `NSCursor.currentSystem` over the probe's own cursors, with its cost and nils. A second process calls it from a background queue: the safe thread, where a crash is the answer.
  - A9: a helper's `NSCursor.hide()` on a shared wall-clock schedule.
  - A10: two 64 × 64 pt streams around the pointer, differenced, and their IoU against the cursor's image.
  - CU-S2's source rows and its ten still starts.
  - CU-S3's ten bursts.
  - CU-S4.
- **posted:** A1–A3, A6 and A7. They run only when `CGPreflightPostEventAccess()` is true in the terminal-run poster (`post` mode); otherwise each is skipped by name. The listener is always the scratch bundle (`listen` mode), never a terminal-run process: a terminal-run listener holds the terminal's grants, not its own.
  - The bundle reports its own grants first. A row whose grant differs from the one it tests is skipped as `scratch bundle holds <grant>`, because TCC is reset only under `--person`. A7 (a key tap under secure input) runs only when the bundle holds Input Monitoring, since a key tap sees no keys without it.
  - The listener bundle is opened before the poster runs, and its answer's `ready_wall` must precede the plan's `start_wall`, or the row is an instrument failure. A poster answering `skipped` skips the row by name.
  - The truth is each window's own count of the events it received. Half go to the bundle's window (the rule's "Frame Job's own windows"), half to a `target` helper's.
- **person** (`--person`: prompts on stderr, waits on Return, and merges its rows into the existing `results.json`):
  - A4's real moves.
  - A5 over TextEdit text, a Safari link and a resize edge.
  - A9 with TextEdit's hide-until-moved.
  - A1–A3 by hand, three times: with no grant, with Input Monitoring only, and with Accessibility only.
  - A8 and A11: each grant pair from a clean state. Before each pair the runner runs `tccutil reset ListenEvent com.kgalligan.FrameJob.cursorspike`, the only `tccutil` call, on that id only. The owner answers y/n for "prompt shown" and "listed in the pane"; the runner opens `Privacy_ListenEvent`. The key count window opens on a go file the runner writes when the owner presses Return to start typing (or on the grant, if that comes later), not when the grant alone is detected: the tap made before the grant and the one made after it then count keys side by side over the same 8 s.
  - CU-S2's picked window, through `SCContentSharingPicker`.

**A locked console.** The `host` mode reads `CGSessionScreenIsLocked`. While the console is locked, every row that needs the screen or an active window is skipped by name. ScreenCaptureKit then records the lock screen, with no window and no menu bar, and nothing activates. CU0b's first runs, made before this check existed, measured the lock screen's animated wallpaper: every frame was dirty edge to edge. The probe's In the picture rows are skipped as `probe not active` when the probe cannot activate within 2 s. Separate's rows do not need it.

**Grants.** No mode asks for a grant except `grant`, which runs only under `--person`. The other modes only read them: `CGPreflightScreenCaptureAccess`, `CGPreflightPostEventAccess`, `CGPreflightListenEventAccess`, `AXIsProcessTrusted` (no prompt option) and `IOHIDCheckAccess`. Every ScreenCaptureKit mode reads Screen Recording first and answers `skipped` without it.

# TX3b — implementation notes (lane A, worktree `wf_3be7d22c-b55-11`)

Base `e18ef4b45eb227c6f7c8848c18256e658d73cabe` (I's HEAD). Caches CoW-copied from I (build, the
three Rust targets, agent/node_modules, tools/proof/media).

## The question (for the orchestrator / owner)

**Measured (Debug, `transcript_cut_proof.py --only P1,P2`, the pause fixture: four `say` phrases
joined by 2.5 s, 1.5 s and 0.8 s of zero samples, clip at 0 ×1, 30 fps):**

- **The 2.5 s gap.** The quiet is [1,627,500, 3,185,775) ticks, measured to the samples over
  −40 dBFS. The span is [1,766,400, 3,187,200), which is 2.37 s. The unclamped cut would be
  [1,880,000, 3,060,000). The next word, "Pack", starts at 2,520,000 on this Mac's E0 words, which
  is 1.11 s before its audible onset. That start lies inside [s, e), so step 3 moves s to
  2,540,000. The cut is therefore [2,540,000, 3,060,000), 0.87 s. After the tab's Delete Pause, the
  tool still answers a pause after "dog": span [1,766,400, 2,534,400) (1.28 s, shown "[1.3 s]"),
  cut [1,880,000, 2,420,000).
- **The 1.5 s gap.** The same thing happens. "How" starts 1.07 s before its audible onset, so the
  cut is [4,940,000, 5,460,000) instead of starting at 4,840,000. After the delete, a 1.44 s pause is
  still answered.
- **What still holds.** Everything else in P2 passes: `in_out_range` is the cut, the undo is named
  "Delete Pause", the tab's placements equal `ripple_delete_ranges` of the tool's
  `cut_start`/`cut_end`, and every word id is kept.

TX-S3 recorded E0 as always early, by 110–1,186 ms. So on on-device words the word after a gap
usually starts inside the silence, and this is the common case, not an edge.

**Options:**

- **(a) Keep step 3 as written.** The cut takes the silence from the word after's transcript start,
  so a pause can only shrink. It can stay over 1 s, as both pauses here do. A second ⌫ on the
  remaining token cuts the part before that start. P2 and the Goal's "shortens it to 0.2 s each end"
  would be restated as "shortens it; a second Delete may be needed when the word after starts early".
- **(b) Cut straight through b's transcript start**, `[span + 0.2 s, span − 0.2 s)`. This meets the
  Goal, but b's source start leaves every clip window. The word drops out of the transcript while its
  sound stays: the sliver/vanishing-word problem TX-30's snapping rule exists to prevent (TX3a C2).
- **(c) Two ranges in one `ripple_delete_ranges`:** `[s, frameFloor(b.start))` and
  `[frame after b.start, e)`. This meets the Goal and keeps b in the transcript, but leaves a
  one-frame, silent clip holding b's start on every unlocked track. The clip count and peak grow by
  the extra split.

**Recommendation: (c).** It is the only option that delivers what TX-34 promises, a pause shortened
to 0.2 s each end, without losing a word from the transcript. The silent one-frame sliver is
inaudible. Its timeline clutter is the cost, and it should be named in TX-34 and JOB-11. If the
owner prefers no slivers, (a) is the honest fallback, with the Goal and P2 restated.

# FC3 (lane A): implementation notes

- Base: `59e8546579efc00a49bbcc4ed31d1ea014c84b77` (I's HEAD). Tip: `64b743551a1c201d6ed7a1a9cdc056a2ebaf1c9e`.

- Caches were copied from I as `cj-lanes-common.md` says: build, the three targets, agent/node_modules and tools/proof/media.

## What was done
- Head instruments, committed at the tip, and nothing else:
  - `tools/proof/creator_spike/sound_spike.swift`: the `labels` and `run <file> <window> file|stream` modes, built over `app/Sources` through `swift_build.build`. The stream mode feeds `SNAudioStreamAnalyzer` from `MediaImporter.speechReader`'s 16 kHz mono float decode of the first audio track (`CompositionBuilder.assetTrack`). Overlap is 0.5.
  - `tools/proof/creator_spike/sound_deciders.py`: the rule as pure functions, with 12 `--selftest` rows that all pass. It includes the agreeing and disagreeing agreement rows the spec asks for.
  - `tools/proof/creator_spike/sound_spike.py`: the runner. It checks the rule (`rule_sha256` matches CJ0a's table), writes the say fixtures and the 10-min `-stream_loop` of the Rode file, times 3 windows × 2 analyzers × 3 runs, checks agreement on every input and window, checks determinism, writes `results.json` and prints the VERDICT line.
- One deviation in `window_rule`: the rule's "if none reaches 60×, the slowest acceptable is kept" is implemented as "the fastest is kept". That reading is a guess. The case did not arise, since every window ran above 218×.

## The run (on AC, M2 Max, macOS 26.5.1 25F80)
`VERDICT window=1.5 hop=0.75 groups=weak(all, no S-EV) labels=all stream_agrees=no deterministic=yes rt_1.0_file=218.6 rt_1.0_stream=229.5 rt_1.5_file=276.4 rt_1.5_stream=297.6 rt_3.0_file=353.7 rt_3.0_stream=390.3`

- **Labels:** all 11 FC-31 labels are in `.version1`'s 303 known classifications. The window constraint is a range of 0.5–15 s, and 1.0, 1.5 and 3.0 s are set exactly.
- **Speed:** every window × analyzer is far above 60× (medians above), so the window rule keeps 1.5 s (no S-EV recall, so it falls to the tie rule). The hop is 0.75 s.
- **Determinism:** the three stream runs at each window gave byte-identical values (sha256).
- **Agreement:** it fails under the deciders' definition: every group, every input, every window length, each rising 0.5 crossing matched within one hop in both directions.
  - 1.0 s: `filler` has 1 unmatched crossing and the 10-min Rode loop has 4 (music). The other inputs agree.
  - 1.5 s, the window kept: every input agrees.
  - 3.0 s: the 10-min loop has 1 unmatched crossing (speech at 312 s). The other inputs agree.
- **Why it fails** (the diagnostic is in `FC-S1-near-threshold.log`): every unmatched crossing is one window where the two analyzers sit on either side of 0.5.
  - The pairs are 0.501/0.498, 0.511/0.495, 0.507/0.493, 0.437/0.525 and 0.458/0.506.
  - Over whole files, |file − stream| has a median of 0.003–0.009 and a maximum of 0.05–0.09.
  - The times agree. The values differ slightly, presumably because the file analyzer resamples the source itself while the stream is fed AVAssetReader's 16 kHz resample.
- **S-EV, S-TH1/S-ST1 and S-MU** are skipped by name and owed. Every group is weak by rule.
- Evidence in the handoff dir: `FC-S1-results.json` (the results file, `rule_matches: true`), `FC-S1-near-threshold.log` and `04-checks.txt`.

## The question for the designer, then the owner
FC-S1's rule says the stream analyzer is used "if its event times agree with the file analyzer's within one hop". The spec turned that into an exact 0.5-crossing match, which a 0.003 difference at the threshold breaks. The options:
- **(a) Amend the agreement metric with a value tolerance.** A crossing counts as matched when the other side has a crossing within one hop, OR its value in that window is within ±0.1 of 0.5 (hysteresis). The tolerance would be set from these measurements before any re-run. Under it, all 7 unmatched crossings would match, so the stream analyzer agrees.
- **(b) Apply the agreement rule only at the window FC-30 keeps (1.5 s).** It agrees there on every input as measured. The rule as written says every window length.
- **(c) Take the rule's own fallback: the file analyzer.** The kind's version records `file`, and FC-31 is amended. `SNAudioFileAnalyzer` reads the whole file. It cannot analyse a missing range, and it does not skip an MP3's encoder delay through `MP3Gapless.leadingTrim`. FC-31's ranges, `readWindow`, P4, P6, P9 and E4 would all need redesigning.
- **Recommendation: (a), else (b).** The times agree and the values differ in the third decimal. The stream path is what keeps per-range jobs and the MP3 trim. Option (a) also keeps the "every window" scope of the rule fixed at CJ0a.

  - Make two false starts, like "So the main— so what I mean is…".
  - Leave your natural ums and uhs in.
  - Pause once for about 3 seconds.
- **Physical moments, after the first minute. Note each one's rough time:**
