# Recording day: the talking head (CP1) and the screen tutorial (CU12)

There are two recordings. The talking head comes first, because it unblocks the most work: transcript editing TX4–TX7, then Find Clips and multi-track audio. If you have time while the camera is set up, a few short extra clips at the end pay off checks that are already owed.

Everything goes under `tools/proof/media/creator/` in the creator-jobs worktree, `~/devel/framejob/.claude/worktrees/creator-jobs/`. That folder is gitignored and never committed. Keep camera files exactly as they came off the card: don't re-encode, trim or rename them.

**Privacy.** Two paid tests use the talking head: AssemblyAI gets its audio and Anthropic gets its transcript text. Say only what you're fine sending to them.

---

## Before you start (5 minutes)

1. **Build the app once and use that build all day.** The lanes keep landing changes.
   ```sh
   cd ~/devel/framejob/.claude/worktrees/creator-jobs
   make app
   open "build/Build/Products/Release/Frame Job.app"
   ```
2. **Permissions** (System Settings ▸ Privacy & Security). Give **Frame Job** Screen Recording, Microphone and Camera.
   - Also give it **Input Monitoring**, for the tutorial's shortcut capture. macOS shows no prompt for this and doesn't list Frame Job. Add it with **+**, from the build above.
   - A new build can lose these permissions. If recording refuses, re-check them.

---

## 1. Talking head: S-TH1, your trial video T1 (about 6 minutes)

**Aim for an ordinary video of the kind you'd actually make, not a studio piece.** Real stumbles are the point. Talk about something real, such as Frame Job or a topic you know, because you'll cut this to a publishable state afterwards.

**Camera: GH5**
- **Profile:** standard (Rec. 709), **not** V-Log.
- **Format:** 4K, 30p.
- **Framing:** head and shoulders, eye level, a little headroom.
- **Lighting:** normal decent light from a window or a key light. Not backlit.
- **Background:** an ordinary room is good, clutter included, because it tests the cutout.

**Sound**
- Record the **RØDE as its own file** at the same time. Use Frame Job (File ▸ New Recording… ⌥⌘N, Source **Microphone Only**) or QuickTime.
- Keep the camera's own sound too.
- **Clap once** at the start.

**Script of moments.** Keep it natural, and **write down the rough time of each physical moment**.

- **0:00–1:00:** face the camera and just talk. Nothing unusual happens in this minute.
- **After the first minute, work these in:**
  - Say **three lines twice**: a flubbed take, then a good one.
  - Make **two false starts**, like "So the main— so what I mean is…".
  - Leave your **natural ums and uhs** in.
  - Make **one ~3-second pause**.
- **The physical moments, each noted with its time:**
  - Lean out of frame once.
  - Stand up and leave for about 3 s.
  - Turn away from the camera for about 5 s.
  - Give one side-on beat (profile).

**Files.** In `S-TH1/`:
- the camera file, untouched;
- the RØDE file;
- `notes.txt` with the times of the moments above.

### Then: checkpoint CP1, cutting T1 by text

1. Open the camera file in Frame Job (File ▸ Open…). Add the RØDE file and line them up with **Clip ▸ Synchronize Audio**.
2. **View ▸ Transcript** (⌃⌘T), and wait for the words.
3. Cut it to a state you'd publish, **only by editing the text**:
   - select words (click, drag, ⇧-click);
   - listen with Loop;
   - press **⌫** to cut;
   - click a pause token like `[2.4 s]` and press ⌫ to shorten it;
   - undo whatever sounds wrong.
4. **Write down, as you go:**
   - each time you left for the timeline or another tool, and why;
   - each slow step;
   - each cut that **sounded wrong**, with its time: a clipped start, a leftover fragment, an unnatural pause, or the end of the previous word eaten;
   - what you wanted from the transcript that it didn't give you.
5. Do manual check **JOB-11** in `docs/manual-checks.md` on the same recording. It's a dozen single-word cuts plus a few pause cuts, listening across each one.

Send me the notes. TX4 onward starts on your verdict.

---

## 2. Screen tutorial: CU12, your screen-tutorial trial (10–20 minutes)

A real narrated tutorial: something you'd actually show someone, in any app.

**Record it with Frame Job** (File ▸ New Recording… ⌥⌘N):

| Setting | Value |
|---|---|
| Source | your main display (not Window…) |
| Microphone | the RØDE |
| Record the camera too | on (GH5 or iPhone; Layout: Corner) |
| Cursor | **Separate** (the default for a display) |
| Show Clicks | on |
| Record shortcuts | **on** (needs Input Monitoring, see above) |
| When it lands: Zoom in on clicks | on |
| When it lands: Show shortcuts | on |
| When it lands: Speed up typing | off (try it by hand afterwards) |
| Enhance the microphone when it lands | your choice (on is a good test) |

**While recording, do what a tutorial naturally has:**
- clicks across different parts of the screen;
- some typing;
- **at least two keyboard shortcuts**;
- some scrolling;
- a mistake or two that you correct.

### Then: cut it with the new tools, and time yourself

1. Let it land. The zooms and shortcut overlays are applied automatically.
2. **Manual check JOB-25 (Auto Zoom).**
   - Play it through. Were the zooms where you'd have put them? Note any that came too early, too late, too tight, too often, or were missing.
   - Then undo, and try **Clip ▸ Auto Zoom…** at Zoom 1.5× and again at Stay 4 s. Which reads better?
3. Finish the cut with the rest:
   - the Cursor section: size and style, plus **Polish** for smoothing and hide-when-idle;
   - **Clip ▸ Speed Up Typing…**;
   - motion blur on the zooms;
   - camera layouts (Clip ▸ Camera Layout ▸);
   - the Transcript tab for wording.
4. **Write down:**
   - total time to a cut you'd publish;
   - what you had to redo by hand;
   - what you'd change;
   - your verdict.

   For a comparison, estimate how long the same cut would have taken by hand, with hand-placed Zoom to Region and no overlays. If you have time, really cut the first 5 minutes by hand first, on a duplicate.

**Files.** In `S-ST3/`: the recording's movie files **with their `.fjcursor` files** beside them. They are in the project package, or where Frame Job saved the recording. Copy the whole set.

---

## 3. Optional while you're set up (about 10 minutes total)

Each clip pays off checks that are already owed. Put each in its own folder under `tools/proof/media/creator/`.

| Folder | What | Length |
|---|---|---|
| `S-TH2/` | Same GH5 setup, **V-Log L**, 4K 25p 10-bit | ~2 min |
| `S-TH3/` | iPhone 18 Pro in **Apple Log** | ~1 min |
| `S-TH4/` | iPhone 18 Pro at its **defaults** (HDR): 1 min landscape + 20 s portrait | ~1.5 min |
| `S-TH5/` | Hard cases for cutout: backlit by a window, hair against a busy background, turned away, small in frame | ~1 min |
| `S-KEY1/` | Either camera, 1080p30, in front of an evenly lit plain cloth (green, blue or any saturated colour unlike your skin and clothes): 15 s still, 20 s gesturing, 15 s turning your head | ~1 min |
| `S-ST2/` | Another short screen tutorial with **Cursor: In the picture** (compares the burned pointer with the cursor file) | 5–10 min |
| `S-ST4/` | A **Window…** recording where you drag and resize the window while recording | 1–2 min |

**Later, and not tomorrow:**
- **Two-person podcast samples** (S-PC1, S-PC2, S-PC3) need a second person.
- **S-RT1** needs a retake script that a later phase writes.
- **S-LONG1** is an hour-plus recording.

# Recording guide (iPhone 18 Pro edition, 2026-11-06)

**Where files go:** `/Users/kevingalligan/devel/framejob/.claude/worktrees/creator-jobs/tools/proof/media/creator/<sample>/`, with one folder per sample (`S-TH1/`, `S-ST3/`, and so on).
- This is the creator-jobs worktree. Main's `tools/proof/media/` is a different folder, and the lanes don't read it.
- The folder is gitignored, so nothing in it is ever committed.
- Keep camera files exactly as they came off the phone: don't re-encode, trim, rename, or export them from Photos.

**Getting files off the iPhone untouched:**
1. Set iPhone **Settings ▸ Photos ▸ Transfer to Mac or PC** to **Keep Originals**.
2. Connect a USB-C cable and use **Image Capture** on the Mac. It's the safest route, especially for ProRes.
- AirDrop also works if you pick **Options ▸ All Photos Data** in the share sheet.

**Privacy:** two paid tests send S-TH1 out: its audio to AssemblyAI and its transcript text to Anthropic. Say only what you're fine sending. A guest's voice is sent only with their agreement.

---

## Storage on the phone (about 110 GB free)

| Mode | About | 110 GB holds |
|---|---|---|
| ProRes **Log**, 4K 30 | 6–7 GB a minute | about 15 minutes |
| ProRes Log, 1080p 30 | 1.7 GB a minute | about 60 minutes |
| HEVC (High Efficiency), 4K 30, SDR or HDR | about 0.2 GB a minute | hours |

Today's whole iPhone plan below comes to **about 10 GB**. Only one sample, S-TH3, needs Log.

**S-TH1 is NOT recorded in Log.** Its job is the standard-picture baseline: the cut, faces, cutout and framing all start from it. S-TH3 is the separate Log sample, compared against it. Six minutes of Log would also be about 40 GB, against about 1.2 GB in HEVC.

---

## The iPhone settings each sample uses

**A. "Standard" (SDR, constant 30 fps):** S-TH1, S-TH5 and S-KEY1.
1. **Settings ▸ Camera ▸ Formats:**
   - High Efficiency.
   - Apple ProRes **off**.
2. **Settings ▸ Camera ▸ Record Video:**
   - **4K at 30 fps** (1080p at 30 fps for S-KEY1).
   - **HDR Video off.**
   - **Auto FPS off**, so the frame rate stays constant.
   - **Lock Camera on**, so the phone doesn't switch lenses mid-take.
   - Enhanced Stabilization off; you're on a tripod.
3. **In the Camera app:**
   - Use the rear main camera (1×).
   - Use Video mode, not Cinematic or Action.
   - Before you start, press and hold on your face to lock focus and exposure.

**B. "Log":** S-TH3 only.
- Settings ▸ Camera ▸ Formats: turn Apple ProRes **on** and choose **Log** for its encoding.
- Use 4K 30. Everything else is as in A.
- If your Formats screen offers Log with High Efficiency instead of ProRes, that's fine too, and much smaller.

**C. "Defaults" (HDR, HLG, variable frame rate):** S-TH4 only.
- High Efficiency, **HDR Video on**, **Auto FPS on**, ProRes off. These are the phone's out-of-the-box settings.

Put settings back to A when you're done with B or C.

---

## Today, in order

### 1. S-TH1: the talking head, your trial video T1 (6–7 min, settings A) ★ the important one

This one unblocks the most work: transcript editing TX4–TX8, Find Clips, multi-track audio and linked versions.

**Aim for an ordinary video you'd actually make, not a studio piece.** Real stumbles are the point. Talk about something real, because you'll cut it into something publishable afterwards.

**Camera and set:**
- iPhone on a tripod, landscape, at eye level; head and shoulders with a little headroom.
- Decent ordinary light, from a window to your side or a lamp. Not backlit.
- An ordinary room with clutter behind you is good: it tests the cutout.

**Sound:**
- Record the **RØDE as its own file at the same time**: Frame Job, **File ▸ New Recording… (⌥⌘N)**, Source **Microphone Only**.
- The iPhone records its own sound too; keep it.
- **Clap once** at the start, visible to the camera, so the two line up.

**What to do.** Keep it natural, and **write down the rough time of each physical moment** as you go.

- **0:00–1:00:** face the camera and just talk. Nothing unusual happens in this first minute.
- **After the first minute, work these in:**
  - Say **three lines twice**: a flubbed take, then a good one.
  - Make **two false starts**, like "So the main— so what I mean is…".
  - Leave your **natural ums and uhs** in.
  - Make **one pause of about 3 seconds**.
- **Physical moments, each with its time noted:**
  - Lean out of frame once.
  - Stand up and walk out of frame for about 3 seconds.
  - Turn away from the camera for about 5 seconds.
  - Give one side-on (profile) beat.

**In `S-TH1/`:**
- the iPhone movie, untouched;
- the RØDE file;
- `notes.txt`, with the times of the moments and "iPhone 18 Pro, SDR HEVC 4K30 (GH5 in storage)".

#### Then CP1: cut T1 by editing its text

1. Build the app from the worktree once and use that build all day:
   ```sh
   cd ~/devel/framejob/.claude/worktrees/creator-jobs
   make app
   open "build/Build/Products/Release/Frame Job.app"
   ```
2. Open the iPhone movie, add the RØDE file, and line them up with **Clip ▸ Synchronize Audio**.
3. Open **View ▸ Transcript (⌃⌘T)** and wait for the words.
4. Cut it to a state you'd publish, **only by editing the text**:
   - select words by click, drag or ⇧-click;
   - listen with Loop;
   - press **⌫** to cut;
   - click a pause token like `[2.4 s]` and press ⌫ to shorten it;
   - undo whatever sounds wrong.
5. **Write down as you go:**
   - each time you left for the timeline or another tool, and why;
   - each slow step;
   - each cut that **sounded wrong**, with its time: a clipped start, a leftover fragment, an odd pause, the end of the previous word eaten;
   - what you wanted from the transcript and didn't get.
6. Run manual check **JOB-11** in `docs/manual-checks.md` on the same recording: about a dozen single-word cuts and a few pause cuts, listening across each one.

Send me the notes. TX4 onward starts on your verdict.

### 2. Quick iPhone extras while the tripod is up (about 5 min of recording, about 8 GB)

| Folder | Settings | What to record | Length |
|---|---|---|---|
| `S-TH3/` | **B (Log)** | The same framing as S-TH1, just talking | 1 min (~6–7 GB) |
| `S-TH4/` | **C (Defaults)** | Talking to the camera in **landscape**, then the phone turned **portrait** | 1 min, then 20 s |
| `S-TH5/` | A | Hard cases for the cutout, about 15 s each: backlit by a window; hair against a busy background; turned away; small in frame (step well back) | 1 min |
| `S-IP1/` | A, plus **Settings ▸ Camera ▸ Record Sound ▸ Spatial Audio** on | Anything with talking | 20–30 s |

Afterwards, put Record Sound back to what it was.

### 3. CU12: the screen-tutorial trial (10–20 min; on the Mac, so no phone storage)

A real narrated tutorial: something you'd actually show someone, in any app.

Use the iPhone as the camera beside the screen through **Continuity Camera**. Put the phone near the Mac on a stand, landscape and locked, and it appears in the recorder's camera list. Continuity Camera records to the Mac, not to the phone.

**Record it with Frame Job (File ▸ New Recording… ⌥⌘N):**

| Setting | Value |
|---|---|
| Source | your main display (not Window…) |
| Microphone | the RØDE |
| Record the camera too | on: the iPhone (Continuity Camera), Layout: Corner |
| Cursor | **Separate** (the default) |
| Show Clicks | on |
| Record shortcuts | **on** |
| When it lands: Zoom in on clicks | on |
| When it lands: Show shortcuts | on |
| When it lands: Speed up typing | off (try it by hand afterwards) |
| Enhance the microphone when it lands | your choice; on is a good test |

- **Record shortcuts needs Input Monitoring.** In System Settings ▸ Privacy & Security ▸ Input Monitoring, add **Frame Job** with **+**, picking the build from step 1. macOS shows no prompt for this. Also give it Screen Recording, Microphone and Camera.
- **A rebuilt app can lose these permissions.** If recording refuses, check them again.

**While recording, include what a tutorial naturally has:**
- clicks in different parts of the screen;
- some typing;
- **at least two keyboard shortcuts**;
- some scrolling;
- a mistake or two that you correct.

**Then cut it with the new tools, and time yourself:**
1. Let it land. The zooms and shortcut overlays are applied automatically.
2. **JOB-25 (Auto Zoom):**
   - Play it through and note zooms that came too early, too late, too tight, too often, or were missing.
   - Undo, and try **Clip ▸ Auto Zoom…** at Zoom 1.5×, and again at Stay 4 s. Which reads better?
3. Finish the cut with:
   - the Cursor section: size, style, and **Polish** for smoothing and hide-when-idle;
   - **Clip ▸ Speed Up Typing…**;
   - motion blur on the zooms;
   - **Clip ▸ Camera Layout ▸**;
   - the Transcript tab for wording.
4. **Write down:**
   - total time to a cut you'd publish;
   - what you had to redo by hand;
   - what you'd change;
   - your verdict;
   - a guess at how long the same cut would take by hand.

**In `S-ST3/`:** the recording's movie files **with their `.fjcursor` files** beside them, copied as a set from the project package or from wherever Frame Job saved the recording.

### 4. Optional, Mac only, any time

| Folder | What | Length |
|---|---|---|
| `S-ST2/` | Another narrated tutorial with **Cursor: In the picture**, to compare the drawn pointer with the cursor file | 10–20 min |
| `S-ST4/` | A **Window…** recording: drag and resize the window while recording. It now defaults to the Separate cursor. Then run **JOB-27** | 1–2 min |
| `S-MU/` | You talking over music playing from a speaker, recorded on the RØDE | 2 min |
| `S-KEY1/` | Settings A at **1080p 30**, in front of an evenly lit plain cloth (green, blue, or any saturated colour unlike your skin and clothes): 15 s still, 20 s gesturing, 15 s turning your head with hair visible, 10 s leaning out of frame | 1 min |

---

## Later: these need a second person or the GH5

| Folder | What to record | Needs |
|---|---|---|
| `S-PC3/` | **Two people in ONE wide shot** (one camera framing both), **a microphone each** on separate files, 3–5 min of natural conversation, a clap at the start. The iPhone works (settings A). | A guest, plus a second mic: a second USB mic, a lavalier into another recorder, or any device writing its own file |
| `S-PC1/` | Two people, **a camera on each** (GH5 on one, iPhone on the other, plus a wide if a third camera is to hand), a mic each, and a lavalier on each too if you have two; 15–20 min **with crosstalk and laughter**. An agent drafts `turns.json` (turn markers over five minutes) for you to correct. | GH5 (or a second camera), a guest |
| `S-PC2/` | Two people **sharing ONE microphone**, a camera on each, each also wearing a lavalier, 5–10 min | Two cameras, a guest |
| `S-EV/` | About 8 min of you talking to camera while someone **off-mic** laughs, claps and cheers, at least 20 times each, with a written list of each event's start to the second | A second person |
| `S-TH2/` | The S-TH1 set-up on the **GH5 in V-Log L**, 4K 25 10-bit | GH5 |
| `S-LONG1/` | Any recording an hour or longer (an extended S-PC1, or a long talk) | Time |
| `S-RT1/` | A retake script read on the RØDE, 3–5 min | A later phase writes the script |

A two-person sample needs your guest's agreement before their voice goes to a paid service. Note it in the folder.

## Road map "creator-jobs" CJ7 — S-TH1's owed rows (`creator_spike/sth1.py`; the S-TH1 arms of the spikes, `faces_proof.py` F5, `creator_spike/audio_tracks.py` SW-S1 (f))

S-TH1 is the owner's talking head (`samples/README.md`), in
`tools/proof/media/creator/S-TH1/` (untracked): `IMG_0181.MOV` (an iPhone 18 Pro Max, 4K 30 HEVC
SDR, stored upside down, a −180 rotation; AAC stereo, a 4-channel APAC track and six metadata
tracks), `IMG_0181.aifc` (the RØDE) and `notes.txt` (the owner's beat times). `sth1.py` is what
every arm reads: `movie()` pinned to `IMG_0181.MOV` by name (never a suffix pick: the side-on
add-on lands in the same folder), `addon(folder)` the add-on, `facts()` an ffprobe re-measure,
`BEATS` (lean out, leave, look away) and `ABSENT` (the empty chair at the start and the end) as
whole-second spans read from autorotated `fps=1` frames, `face_present(t)` outside both, and
`profile_span(samples)` the longest run after 10 s with no face at |yaw| < π/4 − 0.01. Every arm
writes `tools/proof/work/creator_spike/<ID>-STH1/results.json` through `rule.write_results`
(the spike's own `rule_sha256`, `sth1_facts` and the spans), leaving the spike's earlier
`results.json` untouched, and prints a `VERDICT` line or `SKIP <row>: <reason>`.

```sh
python3 tools/proof/creator_spike/sth1.py                       # the facts, the spans, the add-on
python3 tools/proof/creator_spike/faces_spike.py --sth1         # CJ-S2 rules 3 and 6 (CJ-S2-STH1)
python3 tools/proof/creator_spike/subjects_spike.py --sth1 --addon-dir <I>/tools/proof/media/creator/S-TH1   # VR-S1 rules 2 and 4 (VR-S1-STH1)
python3 tools/proof/creator_spike/shots_spike.py --socket <sock>   # CJ-S4 with S-TH1 as the no-cut input (CJ-S4-STH1)
python3 tools/proof/creator_spike/sound_spike.py --sth1         # FC-S1's speech-only calls (FC-S1-STH1)
python3 tools/proof/creator_spike/audio_tracks.py [--movie PATH]   # SW-S1 (f) (SW-S1-f)
python3 tools/proof/cutout_spike/cutout_spike.py --only s1-sth1 --device gpu   # CO-S1's speed rows (CO-S1-STH1), about 30 minutes
python3 tools/proof/transcript_spike/fill_spike.py --part owner   # TX-S1 on S-TH1, one run per call (TX-S1-STH1)
python3 tools/proof/transcript_spike/cut_spike.py               # TX-S3 with S-TH1 (TX-S3-STH1)
make app && python3 tools/proof/proof_app.py launch --app release
python3 tools/proof/creator_spike/reframe_spike.py --sth1 --socket <dir>/agent.sock   # VR-S2 (VR-S2-STH1)
RC_PROOF_APP=release python3 tools/proof/faces_proof.py --only F5   # F5 on S-TH1
```

`audio_tracks_probe.swift` is built alone; it prints each `tracks(withMediaType: .audio)` row
(track ID, the FourCC, channels, rate, title, enabled, whether one float LPCM buffer decodes) and
the other tracks' counts, and `audio_tracks.py` sets ffprobe's audio streams beside it. The
recorded runs, the rows skipped and those still owed are in `designs/creator-jobs.md`'s
